- Model consistently underestimates prices after strong sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment > 0.8) — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for such periods.
- After a sharp price spike, model overreacts and overshoots — cap forecast at +2% above recent peak or use moving average to smooth.
- When sentiment is negative or low (e.g., < 0.5), model fails to anticipate sharp downward moves — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if price has been trending upward for 5+ days, forecast should not continue rising beyond 10% above recent high.
- Forecast horizon 30d is overly optimistic in early 2023 — reduce baseline by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.2–0.4) over 3+ days, model should not forecast upward trend — expect 1–2% downward correction.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating 0.8 and 0.1), model should not follow trend — use 7-day rolling average to filter noise.
